name: Role Classes
description: Adds one configurable CSS class to the <body> tag, chosen from the current user's highest-weight role.
project_description:
Role Classes is a lightweight Drupal module that automatically adds a single CSS class to the <body> tag based on the current user's highest-privilege role. This lets site builders and theme developers style pages differently per role using pure CSS — no JavaScript, no template overrides, no custom theme hooks required.

How it works: every Drupal role has a weight reflecting its privilege level. On each page request the module reads the current user's roles, picks the one with the highest weight, looks up the CSS class configured for that role, sanitizes it, and appends it to the <body> tag. A user holding multiple roles (e.g. authenticated and editor) receives only the class for the highest-weight role, keeping the markup clean and predictable.

Features: highest-weight role wins (only one class is ever added); fully configurable from an admin form at Admin -> Configuration -> System -> Role Classes; class names validated against the CSS identifier specification and sanitized with Html::cleanCssIdentifier() before output; all logic in a per-request-cached, dependency-injected service (RoleClassesManager) that reads config and loads role entities at most once per request and only for roles that actually have a class configured; ships with a config schema, default configuration and install/uninstall hooks. Compatible with Drupal 10.2+, 11 and 12.

Configuration: navigate to /admin/config/system/role-classes, enter a CSS class name next to each role (leave a field blank to skip that role), and clear caches after saving. Role weights are shown alongside each field so you can follow the privilege hierarchy at a glance.
